Implementation can now attribute any new red to itself rather than to inherited state.

The paper moved again between the seed report (2026-10-15T04:16Z) and this research round: file sha256 553adb31 -> 76a39caf, 3998 -> 4092 lines, paper repo HEAD 5736a967 (dirty) -> b939ccf9 (clean). The task's declared file_scope (9 paths) under-covers the membership-prose audit surface. Eight further files carry membership claims that the live paper now contradicts or that contradict 788's 20-constructor system: docs/reference/axiom-reference.md, docs/project-info/FEATURE_REGISTRY.md, docs/theorem-index.md, typst/chapters/03-proof-theory.typ, FormalSystem/ProofSystem/DerivedAxioms.lean, FormalSystem/Theorems/ConnectDerived.lean, FormalSystem/ProofSystem.lean, docs/user-guide/architecture.md.

C35 coupling is much narrower than the task description feared. None of the nine derived declarations (untilF, fUntilEquiv, discretePropagateFwd, discreteSymmFwd, discretePropagateBwd, connectFuture, tempLinearity, density, z1Thm) is seeded in scripts/lean-citation-manifest.json, so editing their Paper: docstring lines is C35-free. Only FormalSystem/ProofSystem/Axioms.lean is seeded (one entry, keyword_line 486, span 408-534), so only an Axioms.lean edit forces python3 scripts/export-lean-citations.py.

FormalSystem/ProofSystem/README.md still carries the entire pre-788 29-constructor layer table (BX Temporal 9, a '3b. Additional BX Temporal' layer with TL and UT as constructors, Uniformity 4, a Z1 layer, Density 2, Total 29) directly below its own correct sentence saying '20 constructors ... eight layers'. C14 cannot see it twice over: its markdown scope is docs/ plus the ROOT README.md only (nested FormalSystem READMEs are out of scope), and its stale-literal set is {14,21,42,44,45} -- 23 and 29 are not in it. Root README.md:223 is stale the same way and equally invisible.

The paper moved a SEVENTH time, during this planning dispatch: whole-file sha256 76a39caf -> 9c9d8f64 (research round -> plan round), 4092 lines unchanged, paper repo HEAD still b939ccf9 but the file is now DIRTY against it (it was clean at research time). Crucially the anchor-level wave is UNCHANGED: still exactly the same 10 anchors, and all ten NEW per-anchor sha256 values are byte-identical to the research report's Appendix. So the paper's latest edit fell entirely outside the ten drifted blocks -- only the whole-file sentinels (FILE_CHECKSUM, and the clean/dirty posture) moved. Consequence for the plan: the per-anchor hashes are now corroborated by two independent measurements an hour apart, but the three whole-file sentinels must be re-taken at implementation time and this re-pin will pin a DIRTY file, unlike the 27-anchor wave which was the first clean pin since 2026-08-10.

The research report's gate-coupling analysis made phasing mechanical rather than judgmental: C15's theorem-index/declaration binding dictated an atomic-batch phase, C35's single seeded file (Axioms.lean) dictated where export-lean-citations.py runs, and C14's measured blindness dictated that the count-table phase cite an explicit re-derivation from typst-status-counts.sh rather than a gate verdict as its covering check. Phase boundaries fell out of the coupling graph with no guesswork. One report claim was corrected cheaply at plan time: docs/reference/axiom-reference.md IS present in the declared file_scope (verified in state.json), so the under-coverage is seven files not eight; plan-file-scope-harvest.sh over this plan's Files to modify lists yields 18 paths, covering all seven.
Implement dispatch 11 started on a clean working tree (no foreign uncommitted edits outside specs/), so the concurrent-sibling risk the plan flags did not materialize at start.

Phase 1 re-derivation found the paper had moved an eighth time (sha256 9c9d8f64 -> 5fc14b67, 4092 -> 4066 lines, paper HEAD b939ccf9 -> bc010a06). The wave is still 10 red entries but membership changed: def:strongest went from drifted to DANGLING (its \label was removed; Str is now an \aitem key inside def:key-terms) and thm:s5 drifted newly. The three Tier-D hashes moved again; the six BX/TM-core hashes are byte-identical to the hypothesis for the third independent measurement, so the substantive half of the task is unaffected.

The paper moved a NINTH time DURING Phase 2's own execution: sha256 5fc14b67 -> 8a17f609, 4066 -> 4071 lines, between the Phase 1 gate run and the per-anchor --resolve calls minutes later. def:id's NEW hash changed from 36da35ab (Phase 1 measurement) to b52579e8 (write time). Mitigation: the re-pin script asserts each reconstruction against the resolver's own sha at write time, so every write is correct as written; the gate is re-run at the end of Phase 3 and any re-dried anchor is re-resolved into the same drift-correction entry, per the 27-anchor wave's in-flight def:id precedent. The acceptance statement names the revision actually absorbed.

C15's theorem-index cross-check requires the declaration's docstring to read exactly 'Paper: <anchor>' on its own line; a trailing parenthetical reason is tolerated only on the 'Paper: - (reason)' form. The first pass wrote 'Paper: `def:TMplus` (NF is a derived theorem of TM...)' at three declarations and C15 went red with the confusing message 'index row cites def:TMplus but the site reads def:TMplus (...'. Remedy: put the anchor alone on the Paper: line and the explanation in a following paragraph of the same docstring.

Adding lines to a module docstring in FormalSystem/ProofSystem/DerivedAxioms.lean shifted every declaration below it, breaking one C20 declaration-span citation (Tableau.lean:1643 -> DerivedAxioms.lean:253, which now landed in priorSZ instead of priorSGap). reanchor-lean-citations.py --by-name re-pointed 0 citations, so the fix was by hand (253 -> 261). The same edit also staled two generated README inventory blocks, fixed by check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory.

Seven in-tree sites making false claims about the paper's BX/TM axiom membership were outside the plan's per-phase file lists and were absorbed into the phases they belong to: FormalSystem/Metalogic/CompletenessDerived.lean:14, FormalSystem/Theorems/LinearityDerived.lean:14, FormalSystem/ProofSystem/DerivedAxioms.lean:44, FormalSystem/ProofSystem/LinearityDerivedFacts.lean:50, FormalSystem/MinusLanguage/Axioms.lean:65, FormalSystem/ProofSystem/README.md:12, and FormalSystem/README.md:186+190 (TM Base 23 / TM Dense 2 headings). Found by two greps the plan's own Scope Hypotheses prescribed: for 'paper lists|paper schemata|minus the nine|proper subset of', and for the stale literals 23 and 29 next to axiom/constructor/schema.

The mechanical re-pin script (assert the OLD fence against its recorded OLD sha256, reconstruct the NEW text from --resolve, assert the reconstruction against the resolver's own sha, then rewrite fence + sha256 line + MANIFEST row) absorbed eleven re-pins across a paper that moved three times mid-dispatch without a single mis-placed write. It paid for itself the moment def:id had to be re-pinned twice more.

typst-sync-check.sh Check 2 (count freshness) goes red on any edit that changes FormalSystem line counts, because typst/generated/status.typ carries formalsystem-line-count. Regenerating it requires scripts/typst-status-counts.sh WITHOUT --json, and that write path reads axiom sets from the BUILT library -- it refuses with 'could not read axiom sets from the built library. Run lake build first' while a build is in flight. So status.typ regeneration must be sequenced AFTER the full build completes, and typst-sync-check.sh re-run after that. Any Lean docstring edit in this repo therefore implies: build, regenerate status.typ, re-run typst-sync-check.

The plan's Phase 7 named 'bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 4 .' as the task-reference lint that applies in this consumer repo, reasoning that only gate 3 SKIPs outside the source store. Measured: gate 4 SKIPs here too -- the invocation returns 'cannot attest: every gate selected by --only-gate 4 skipped or was deferred -- 0 check(s) ran' with exit 2, which is exactly the zero-check-under-filter condition the plan was trying to avoid. The substantive check was run instead via the repo's own lint, bash .claude/scripts/check-task-references.sh: PASS, 0 unexempted occurrences.

This is INHERITED, not self-inflicted: AxiomDischarge.lean is untouched by this task and its import list is byte-identical at the baseline commit 90afe55a2 (verified with git show).
